note: **7 Pelham Crescent, schedule 217 of the 1939 Register, ED letter code RMGB.** The Cartwright women - Kathleen Christina widowed at 60 in the house she kept with her husband in 1921, and both daughters back in it, married, with two small boys. Three bound by number.
source: 1939 Register, ED letter code RMGB, The National Archives RG101/6178A

census.source: 1939 Register, schedule 217, 7 Pelham Crescent, ED letter code RMGB, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6178A - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 1; the index gives her as Kathleen Cc; she was Thomas William Cartwright's wife in this house in 1921 aged 42, and is widowed here at 60 and still in it

1939 Register, schedule 217, 7 Pelham Crescent, ED letter code RMGB, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6178A - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 2; the index gives her as May E K BARBER, which is her three forenames and her married name; she was thirteen in this house in 1921. Her sons Robert A and Peter John are at sub numbers 4 and 5, which settles Barber as her name on the night

1939 Register, schedule 217, 7 Pelham Crescent, ED letter code RMGB, Nottingham registration district 430-3, sub-district 26, The National Archives RG101/6178A - read from the page by A. Hagues; sub number 3; the index gives her as Patience Goddard (Cartwright) (Perkins); she was eight in this house in 1921, born 1913 on that round and July 1912 here. Cartwright is her maiden name, so Goddard and Perkins are two marriages - Goddard taken as the name she bore in September 1939, on the strength of her sister's entry in the same household, where the surname in front is the one borne on the night. Worth confirming against the page
